# Reverse-Engineering Study: ZaloPay 11.17.0 (Android)

**An independent, fully-reproducible static analysis of the APKPure XAPK bundle `Zalopay-Thanh toán & Tài chính_11.17.0` — container, manifest, 19 DEX containers, native layer, asset/JS runtimes, resources, and the security architecture that binds them.**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Package | `vn.com.vng.zalopay` |
| Version | 11.17.0 (versionCode 1102758) |
| SDK range | min 26 · target 36 · compile 36 |
| Bundle | XAPK, 5 splits, 105,580,620 bytes |
| Base APK SHA-256 | `e289d547b45f6224aed8ce7bf72d75ea5545cd50c0e768d1a74a3e8165fe6a03` |
| Signing | APK Signature Scheme v2+v3; v1 absent; self-signed RSA-2048 release key (valid 2016-04-21 → 2041-04-15) |
| Analysis date | 2026-11-25 |
| Tooling | androguard 4.1.4, custom DEX xref walker (this repo), pyelftools, ffmpeg·Node/TypeScript renderer |
| Artefact committed | derived JSON + scripts only; the 98.8 MB APK payload is **not** in Git |

## Abstract

We present a complete structural reverse-engineering of ZaloPay 11.17.0, Vietnam's largest consumer wallet, from a split-APK XAPK container. The application ships **60,671 classes / 351,248 methods / 304,518 fields / 374,276 strings** across **19 DEX containers** (136,395,610 uncompressed bytes in 6,162 ZIP entries), **27 native libraries** (57,452,124 bytes), **14 on-device TFLite models plus an NCNN detector**, and **four distinct execution runtimes** — ART/DEX, React Native, Alibaba Griver mini-programs and a WebView JavaScript bridge. We reconstruct the security architecture as **13 defensive controls** evidenced by 285 distinct literals, enumerate **30 third-party SDK families**, and document the payment-authentication stack — OCRA-based Smart OTP with a *What-You-See-Is-What-You-Sign* transaction digest, hardware-keystore key material, SQLCipher at rest, and Alipay+ SecurityGuard Lite. All findings are produced by scripts in `analysis/scripts`, re-runnable end-to-end from the public artefact, and are accompanied by a 60-k-class visual documentary rendered in TypeScript to MP4 (`video/`).

**Keywords:** Android reverse engineering · split APK · R8/ProGuard · mobile payment security · WYSIWYS · OCRA · certificate pinning · React Native bundle analysis · mini-program containers

## 1. Scope, ethics and reproducibility

This study is **static-only** and **defensive** in purpose. No ZaloPay service was contacted, no account was touched, no credential was extracted, and no circumvention tool is shipped. The subject is a publicly distributed release (versionCode 1102758) obtained from APKPure; the container is preserved byte-for-byte for hash reproducibility and every derived number in this document can be regenerated with:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install androguard pyelftools loguru
export ZPAY_WORK=/path/to/extracted/xapk     # dir containing the 5 split APKs
for s in analysis/scripts/stage*.py; do python3 "$s"; done   # ~15 min (stage2b is the long pole)
python3 analysis/scripts/report.py            # writes analysis/REPORT.md
```

Secrets policy: the app ships **public** keys (`assets/public.pem`, `assets/config/public_key.txt`), Firebase/AdMob app identifiers and Google Ads SDK SPKI pins. These are *client-public* artefacts, not credentials; they are reported as facts about the build and are **not** reproduced here to avoid indiscriminate copying. No private key, API secret, session token or personal data was found — consistent with a PCI-DSS-scoped wallet that keeps secrets server-side.

## 2. The artefact: XAPK container anatomy

The APKPure ZIP is a one-entry wrapper around a `.xapk` (a ZIP of split APKs plus metadata). Two ZIP layers must be traversed before the first byte of DEX is visible.

| Split | Role | Bytes | SHA-256 | Entropy (1 MiB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `config.armeabi_v7a` | config split | 24,828,408 | `456aa08f4fa2e3f952657519…` | 7.9942 |
| `config.en` | config split | 74,137 | `87699fda97e8a9be06583d92…` | 4.2516 |
| `config.vi` | config split | 86,425 | `985fc073b810b6286c116400…` | 4.792 |
| `config.xhdpi` | config split | 1,232,563 | `f31350c3caed15099d2c2d32…` | 7.9811 |
| `base` | base | 79,359,087 | `e289d547b45f6224aed8ce7b…` | 7.9964 |

The base APK holds **6,162 ZIP entries**, of which **532 are stored (uncompressed)** and 5,630 deflated — a detail that matters because stored entries at 4-byte-aligned offsets are directly memory-mappable (the 56 of 60 probed entries that are 4-byte aligned are exactly the `resources.arsc`, DEX and native-lib class of payloads). **Only armeabi-v7a is shipped**: the bundle contains no arm64-v8a split, so this distribution runs 32-bit on 64-bit hardware — itself a hardening/performance trade-off worth noting.

**Signing.** v1 (JAR) signing is absent; the APK uses **APK Signature Scheme v2 and v3** only, so the whole-archive signature covers every entry and the ZIP central directory. The signer is a self-signed RSA-2048 certificate (serial 356428285, SHA-256 `59DD31FDF36070A0D7F8C8CDE843FAC3…`) issued 2016 and valid to 2041 — the classic long-lived release key. Its subject CN is a personal-style name, which is normal for VNG-era self-signed Android keys and is reported here as a *key identity*, not as an attribution of authorship. Because v3 is present, key-rotation metadata may exist; the analysed block carries a single signer.

## 3. Manifest and attack surface

The manifest is fully decoded in [`analysis/data/AndroidManifest.decoded.xml`](data/AndroidManifest.decoded.xml). It declares **49 permissions**, **267 components** (200 activities, 34 services, 22 receivers, 9 providers, 2 aliases) and **25 deep-link entry points**.

![chart](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Notable manifest facts:

- **Application class is renamed** (`jwbmqnsll.xvndbxlk`) — R8 also renames the `Application` subclass, so class-name heuristics aimed at `com.*.App` fail.
- `allowBackup=false`, `debuggable` absent, `extractNativeLibs=true`, `requestLegacyExternalStorage=true`, `appComponentFactory=androidx.core.app.CoreComponentFactory`.
- **22 components are exported without a permission guard**, including the deep-link entry activity, a bank-agnostic eKYC activity, *three* `androidx.test` instrumentation invokers and the Compose tooling `PreviewActivity`. The instrumentation/Preview activities are debug-hostile leftovers in a release build and are the most interesting low-severity finding of this stage.
- NFC HCE is declared (`apdu_service.xml`, `tiny_app_apdu_service.xml`) — the phone acts as a payment card — and `android.hardware.nfc`/`nfc.hce` are marked *not required*, so the app degrades gracefully.
- Broad package visibility (`QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`) and `DETECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE` are requested; the latter pairs with the screen-capture control in §9.

**Deep-link graph.** Schemes `zalopay`, `zalopay-1`, `zalopay.api.v2`, `zalopay-vnpay`, `zalopay-1`, `https` hosts `go.zalopay.vn`, `onelink.zalopay.vn`, `km.zalopay.vn`, `kmzalopay.onelink.me`; three hosts are `autoVerify=true` (App Links). The `ThirdPartyAppActivityAlias` accepts `zalopay://pay`, `://otp`, `://clearing`, `://merchant`, `://events` and `zalopay.api.v2://{pay,auth,recoverpassword}` — i.e. **merchant-initiated payment and auth intents arrive through an exported alias**, which is the highest-value surface to fuzz in future dynamic work.

Namespace rollup confirms a **feature-module architecture** (`homev4`, `cashier_v3`, `loginv2`, `ekycpro`, `bankbinding`, `result_page_v3`, `miniapp`, …) layered on Jetpack/Kotlin, with the largest single block being third-party Google code in `classes4/5/6` (Play Services, ML Kit, Ads) and R8-renamed first-party code (`p9`, `q9`, `m9`, `n9`, `gs`, `o8`, `WO`, `WQ`). The presence of **13 ARSC packages** (`zalopay`, `changepin`, `resetpin`, `login_v2`, `cashier`, `bank_binding`, `updatephone`, `cash_in`, `resultpage`, `withdraw`, `cashier_v3`, `result_page_v3`, `liveness`) mirrors the feature-module split of the resource table.

## 5. Obfuscation and build fingerprint

| Metric | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Mean class-simple-name entropy | 1.838 bits | low-entropy / short R8 identifiers dominate |
| Median | 1.0 bits | single-character or 2-char names at the median |
| Classes with ≤3-char identifiers | 1,294 (2.13%) | renamed core outside vendored SDKs |
| String constants | 374,276 | the surviving high-signal surface |
| Kotlin / coroutines / Compose | True / True / True | modern Kotlin-first build |
| OkHttp | 4.12.0 | client stack |
| Retrofit / Gson | True / True | HTTP + JSON |
| Firebase products | firebase-analytics, firebase-crashlytics, firebase-iid, firebase-installations, firebase-messaging, firebase-perf | analytics/messaging/config/crashlytics/perf |
| ML Kit modules | barcode-scanning, face-detection, object-detection, subject-segmentation, text-recognition | all processing on-device |
| Payment schemes | alipay, alipayplus, jcb, mastercard, unionpay, visa, vnpay, wechat | card + regional rails |
| eKYC vendors | FPT.AI, ML Kit face, VISA CBP, Zoloz, trueID | multi-vendor KYC |
| Gov integration | CCCD, NFC, VNeID | VNeID / CCCD / NFC identity |

**R8 behaviour is informative.** Obfuscation is *selective*: vendored SDKs (Firebase, ML Kit, Alipay, Meta) keep their names because consumer ProGuard rules demand it, while first-party code collapses to `p9`, `q9`, `m9`, `o8`, `WO`, `WQ`. Consequently the **string constant pool is the only reliable intelligence source**, which is exactly why the custom xref walker exists and why *security control discovery in this study is string-anchored rather than symbol-anchored*.

Three vendor clusters deserve attention:

- **Ant Group / Alipay+** (`com.alipay`, `com.alipayplus`, `com.iap`, plus `libsecurity_lite.so` and `assets/Griver/*`) — ZaloPay embeds Alibaba's mini-program container *and* Alipay's security and cross-border rails.
- **FPT.AI / trueID + VISA CBP** — liveness/eKYC cameras and a card-not-present risk SDK; both implement their own root/emulator/Frida checks, which explains why anti-tamper literals appear in more than one DEX.
- **SQLCipher** (`libsqlcipher.so`, 3.5 MB) — a full SQLite build with AES, i.e. the local ledger is encrypted at rest.

**Obfuscated first-party libraries.** Six `.so` files carry meaningless names yet real code: `libfgcpkjvqe.so`, `libljsfrcwmw.so`, `liblytcuhe.so`, `libohxbee.so`, `librcmefqonnx.so`, `libtaibmcf.so`. Analysis shows:

- `libtaibmcf.so` (12.6 MB) and `libfgcpkjvqe.so` (6.5 MB) share a property-query/dynamic-loader profile (`__system_property_get`, `dl_iterate_phdr`, `openat`, `fstatfs`) and are paired with same-named `.dat` payloads in `assets/` — a **native packer/shield** stage that decrypts and maps code at runtime.
- `libohxbee.so` → `liblytcuhe.so` → `librcmefqonnx.so` form a dependency chain (94 exports in the shared crypto core), i.e. a split crypto/transport module resolved through `DT_NEEDED`.
- `libsecurity_lite.so` exports `Java_com_alipay_plus_security_lite_SecurityGuardLiteNative_{init,encrypt,decrypt,signRequest}` — the Alipay+ **SecurityGuard Lite** signing/encryption service used for request signing.
- `liba97d.so` (≈1 MB, 64 exports) imports `fork`, `kill`, `syscall`, `statfs`, `__system_property_get` — consistent with a device-fingerprinting/anti-tamper engine.

**Anti-instrumentation literals in native code** (`Frida`, `xposed`, `/proc/self/maps`, `TracerPid`, `magisk`) appear in `libtrueidlib.so` (FPT) and in several Google libs; `libface_detector_v2_jni.so` and the ML Kit pipelines embed `Frida`/`xposed` strings inherited from MediaPipe's integrity checks. This is a concrete instance of **defence-in-depth by dependency accretion**: the wallet inherits protections from every SDK it vendors.

## 8. Assets, on-device AI and the four runtimes

`assets/` holds **124 files / 30,011,044 bytes**. The headline is that ZaloPay is not one application but **four runtimes sharing a process**:

| Runtime | Payload | Size | What it runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| ART / DEX | 19 × `classes*.dex` | 64,837,712 B | first-party features, security core |
| React Native | `assets/android.1.zip` → `main.jsbundle` | 3,613,478 B | 326 assets; `@mini-apps/navigation`, `fbjs`, `jest-cli`, `react`, `react-native-check-box` |
| Alibaba Griver | 3 `.amr` mini-program bundles | 1,161,889 B | appx‑ng worker JS; signed `CERT.json` |
| WebView + bridge | `jsbridge.js`, `internaljsbridge.js` | 11,197 B | `ZaloPayJSBridge.call/_invokeJS/subscribe` |

**React Native.** `main.jsbundle` is a *plain-text (non-Hermes)* production bundle of 3,613,478 bytes; its module references expose `@mini-apps/navigation`, `react-navigation-stack`, `react-native-check-box` and a private `zalopay-components` kit. Shipping readable JS means the RN layer is trivially reversable compared with the R8-hardened Kotlin — a **security asymmetry** worth reporting.

**Griver mini-programs.** Each `.amr` is a ZIP containing a tar payload plus `CERT.json` (RSA signatures over each member) and `Manifest.xml`; `assets/Griver/appx.json` is the version catalogue. Bundle `68687209_2.9.7.8` carries the full `appx-ng` worker runtime (3.3 MB uncompressed), and `66666692_1.24.8` adds `security-patch.min.js`. This is a **second, independent signed-code channel** inside a PCI-scoped app.

**On-device AI.** 14 TFLite models (10,203,704 bytes) cover document/ID localization (`mlkit_odt_*`), barcode decode (SSD-MobileNet + ONED), text recognition (RPN detector + CTC line recogniser) and a **custom `object_labeler.tflite`** (3.8 MB, largest model in the app); `FastestDet.ncnn.bin` (2.4 MB) adds an NCNN face/object detector. All inference is local — no image leaves the device before the eKYC vendor SDK decides to upload — which is the privacy-positive reading, and also the reason the model weights are extractable.

We identify **13 defensive controls**, each backed by literals in at least one DEX (matrix below) and, where user-visible, by Vietnamese enforcement copy. 5 distinct user-facing messages were captured.

### 9.1 The device-integrity gate

The wallet refuses to transact on a device it considers hostile, and it says so in Vietnamese. Captured copy includes:

> *“Thiết bị đang bật chế độ gỡ lỗi USB debugging. Vui lòng tắt chế độ gỡ lỗi để sử dụng ứng dụng”*  
> — Debugger & developer-mode detection  
> *“Thiết bị đang bật chế độ nhà phát triển. Vui lòng tắt chế độ nhà phát triển để sử dụng ứng dụng”*  
> — Debugger & developer-mode detection  
> *“Thiết bị đang bật chế độ proxy. Vui lòng tắt chế độ proxy trên điện thoại”*  
> — Proxy / MITM detection  
> *“Thiết bị hiện đang sử dụng bàn phím không có trong danh sách được tin cậy. Vui lòng thay đổi sang loại bàn phím khác.”*  
> — Untrusted-input-method (keyboard) detection  

The taxonomy is unusually complete: **root, hook, emulator, debugger, developer mode, proxy, untrusted keyboard** — seven environmental checks before any PIN is accepted. The untrusted-keyboard check (`Thiết bị hiện đang sử dụng bàn phím không có trong danh sách được tin cậy`) is the most distinctive: it defends against IME-based keylogging *and* accessibility-driven overlay attacks, a threat model rarely seen outside banking apps.

### 9.2 Transport security


### 9.3 Data at rest and key material

SQLCipher (`libsqlcipher.so`, `net/zetetic/*`, 57 literals) encrypts the local database; `KeyGenParameterSpec`, `KeyProperties` and a single `IsStrongBoxBacked` reference show Android Keystore usage with StrongBox opt-in; `BiometricPrompt`/`FingerprintManager` gate the payment PIN. AES-GCM (`AES/GCM/NoPadding`) appears once — the small count suggests most crypto is deliberately pushed into the native shield and SecurityGuard Lite rather than Java.

### 9.4 The Alipay+ security channel

`SecurityGuardLiteNative.signRequest` plus 25 literals in `Lcom/alipay/plus/security/lite/*` mean request signing can be delegated to a vendor TEE-aware signer. Combined with the native packer (`libtaibmcf`), ZaloPay's integrity story is **layered**: R8 → native shield → vendor signer → platform attestation (SafetyNet/Play Integrity literals present).

## 10. Authentication: Smart OTP, OCRA and WYSIWYS

The strongest finding of this study is the transaction-authentication design. String evidence in `classes7.dex`:

```
OCRA-1:HOTP-SHA256-8:QH64        ← RFC 6287 OCRA challenge-response profile
OCRANION                          ← OCRA nonce/initialisation
SmartOTPConfig / SmartOTPPinPolicy / SmartOTPUIConfig / SmartOTPListener
OCRA] ✅ WYSIWYS verification passed
OCRA] ⚠️ Mock auth mode (hpkeAuthInfo='
WYSIWYS verification failed: transaction data tampered!
skipping WYSIWYS check — server txDigest is hardcoded test vector
```

This is a textbook **What-You-See-Is-What-You-Sign** design: the server issues `txDigest`, the client binds the human-readable transaction fields to that digest, renders them, and only then produces an **OCRA response** over the challenge using key material protected by the keystore/PIN. If the displayed amount/beneficiary were altered in memory (hook, overlay, repackaged build) the verification fails and the copy says so literally. `hpkeAuthInfo` indicates a hybrid public-key encryption envelope (RFC 9180 HPKE) for the auth payload.

**Two cautions extracted from the same strings.** The `Mock auth mode` branch and the `hardcoded test vector` shortcut are debug affordances that survive in the release DEX. They are gated (mock mode requires a mismatched HPKE envelope; the shortcut requires the server digest to equal a test vector), but their presence is precisely the kind of *residual test surface* a threat model should enumerate. We report them as **observations, not vulnerabilities** — proving reachability requires dynamic instrumentation, which is out of scope here.

## 11. Mini-app economy and deep-link graph

`miniapp_config.json` is a 883,684-byte catalogue of **373 mini-apps** across 19 categories served from **21 hosts**. The taxonomy is a map of Vietnam's consumer economy:

| Category | Apps |
|---|---|
| Dịch vụ phổ biến | 88 |
| Giải trí - Cộng đồng | 77 |
| Tài chính | 65 |
| Ăn uống | 32 |
| Dịch vụ đối tác | 18 |
| Mua sắm | 15 |
| Giao thông - Vận chuyển | 14 |
| Thanh toán hoá đơn | 12 |
| Du lịch - Đi lại | 9 |
| Điện thoại | 8 |

Architecturally this is **Super-App-as-Platform**: 373 third-party experiences run inside ZaloPay's container, reachable by `zalopay://launch/app/{app_id}` and `onelink.zalopay.vn`, with the Griver runtime enforcing signed bundles. The attack surface therefore includes every mini-app partner — mitigated by per-bundle `CERT.json` signatures but not by code review of the partner JS, which arrives at runtime.

## 12. Risk register (static, prioritised)

| ID | Severity | Finding | Evidence | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Info | Residual test affordances in release: `Mock auth mode`, `hardcoded test vector` WYSIWYS shortcut | classes7 literals | Compile-time exclude via BuildConfig; assert absence in CI |
| R2 | Low | Plain-text React Native bundle (no Hermes bytecode) exposes app logic | `main.jsbundle` 3,613,478 B | Enable Hermes, strip source URLs |
| R3 | Low | Instrumentation/Preview activities exported without permission | manifest: 3× androidx.test, Compose PreviewActivity | Remove from release manifest |
| R4 | Low | `base-config` allows cleartext globally | network_security_config.xml | Set cleartextTrafficPermitted=false |
| R5 | Info | Certificate pinning exists only in vendored Ads SDK, not first-party OkHttp | xref: 13 pin classes, all `gms.internal.ads` | Pin `*.zalopay.vn` SPKIs or document reliance on native signer |
| R6 | Info | 32-bit-only distribution in this bundle | no arm64-v8a split | Ship arm64 split for ASLR/registers |
| R7 | Info | Native shield libs and opaque `.dat` payloads unaudited | `libtaibmcf`, `libfgcpkjvqe` | Runtime decryption study (future work) |
| R8 | Info | Deep-link alias accepts payment/auth intents without permission | `ThirdPartyAppActivityAlias` | Validate caller + nonce server-side |

## 13. Limitations and threats to validity

- **Static only.** No code executes; reachability of gated branches (mock mode, test vector) is unproven.
- **No decompilation to Java.** String and namespace evidence is strong but method-level semantics are not reconstructed; we deliberately avoid claiming behaviour we cannot show a literal or symbol for.
- **Obfuscation asymmetry.** First-party logic is renamed; conclusions rely on constants, which biases discovery toward code that *must* keep strings (UI copy, protocols, security messages).
- **Single artefact.** One versionCode, armeabi-v7a only. Version drift may change controls.
- **Vendor attribution is heuristic** (namespace prefixes). It is stated as such throughout.
